paragraphs: This paper studies the balance between fidelity and diversity in diffusion generation through the internal structure of transformer attention. It treats the attention matrix before softmax as an associative memory: a representation of pairwise relationships between input features. This connects attention to questions about which features are retrieved and how stable that retrieval is.

The authors separate this matrix into symmetric and skew-symmetric components. In their interpretation, the symmetric part defines an energy landscape, while the skew-symmetric part drives circulation across that landscape. The symmetric component also supplies an energy formulation from which they derive Hopfield-style measures of feature stability.

The authors observe meaningful correlations between these stability measures and the fidelity–diversity trade-off. They then propose adjusting circulation as a control for that trade-off. The contribution combines an interpretation of attention with a way to influence generation. The reported correlations support the connection between stability and generation behavior, without establishing that stability alone determines either fidelity or diversity.
icml-2026-balancing-fidelity-and-diversi.tldr: Decomposing attention into energy and circulation components yields stability measures and a control for diffusion models’ fidelity–diversity trade-off.

paragraphs: The paper studies repeated selection of user–item pairs when some features on both sides are hidden. Each round reveals only the selected pair’s reward, which depends bilinearly on user and item features through an unknown matrix. Converting this into a standard linear bandit expands the feature space and loses the explicit bilinear structure.

BiRoLF keeps that structure. It extends both observed feature spaces with orthogonal complement bases to accommodate latent information. Doubly robust estimation supplies estimated rewards for unselected pairs, producing matrix-valued pseudo-rewards. A bilinear DR-Lasso estimator then encourages sparsity in components outside the observed feature spaces.

The regret bound scales, up to logarithmic factors, with the square root of the number of rounds times the product of the two effective feature dimensions. Those dimensions include observable features and effective complement dimensions. An exact blockwise update exploits the resulting Gram structure while preserving the full estimation objective. Numerical experiments report strong regret performance and computational gains, supporting the value of retaining bilinear structure throughout estimation and updating.
icml-2026-bilinear-bandits-with-partiall.tldr: BiRoLF handles partially hidden user and item features while preserving bilinear structure, with regret guarantees and reported computational gains.

paragraphs: Unsupervised domain adaptation depends on measuring how a source domain differs from a target domain. This paper questions the common choice of fixing one divergence measure in advance: a measure that works well for one shift can be less suitable for another. It makes both discrepancy estimation and the choice of divergence adaptable.

The proposed Tighter-VR construction inserts a learnable monotone transform with a bounded Lipschitz constant into a variational lower bound. This tightens the representation used to estimate divergence. A likelihood-based criterion then selects the divergence family from data. The framework includes earlier fixed-divergence approaches as special cases and yields more informative, statistically efficient discrepancy estimates.

The theoretical target-risk bound combines transformed source risk, the proposed domain discrepancy, and an ideal-hypothesis residual. Finite-sample guarantees supplement that analysis. Experiments on Office-31, Office-Home, Digits, and VisDA-2017 consistently improve accuracy over strong baselines. These findings support adapting the discrepancy measure to the shift, while the residual term makes clear that discrepancy is only one component of the risk bound.
icml-2026-domain-adaptation-with-adaptiv.tldr: Learning a tighter divergence representation and selecting its family from data improves domain adaptation in the reported benchmarks.

paragraphs: This paper asks how efficiently a pretrained transformer can learn a regression relationship from examples supplied in its context. The analysis concerns nonparametric regression functions with α-Hölder smoothness, where α is positive. Smoothness restricts how irregular the relationship can be, and the input dimension d also enters the statistical guarantee.

With n examples in context, the authors show that a transformer with Θ(log n) parameters can achieve mean squared error O(n^(-2α/(2α+d))). This is the minimax optimal convergence rate for the studied setting. Their result uses Ω(n^(2α/(2α+d)) log³ n) pretraining sequences and requires substantially fewer parameters and pretraining sequences than earlier theoretical results.

The construction works by efficiently approximating local polynomial estimators. The transformer implements a kernel-weighted polynomial basis and then performs gradient descent. This gives a concrete computational route from attention-based machinery to an optimal statistical estimator. The claim establishes that a suitably pretrained transformer can attain the rate under the stated smoothness setting; it does not assert that arbitrary transformers automatically do so.
icml-2026-efficient-and-minimax-optimal-.tldr: A theoretical transformer construction achieves minimax-optimal in-context regression with logarithmically many parameters under Hölder smoothness.

paragraphs: Importance sampling estimates expectations under a target distribution by drawing samples from a proposal distribution and assigning them weights. Its efficiency depends strongly on how well that proposal matches the target. The problem becomes particularly challenging for complex targets with multiple modes in high-dimensional spaces, where a poorly adapted proposal can make sampling inefficient.

The paper develops an adaptive method for constructing better proposals. It combines global sampling mechanisms with a delayed weighting procedure, linking exploration to the way samples receive their weights. The delayed weighting mechanism enables rapid resampling in regions where the current proposal is poorly adapted to the target distribution.

The authors prove geometric convergence under assumptions they describe as mild and illustrate the algorithm through numerical experiments. The convergence result is conditional on those assumptions. The broader contribution is a sampling design in which proposal adaptation and weighting work together: global sampling promotes exploration, while the weighting procedure helps redirect resampling toward regions needing better adaptation.
icml-2026-entropic-mirror-monte-carlo-7d.tldr: An adaptive importance sampler combines global exploration with delayed weighting and achieves geometric convergence under stated assumptions.

paragraphs: EvoCF addresses collaboration planning for embodied agents, where a plausible language-model plan can still fail because it overlooks physical or coordination constraints. The framework searches for improved strategies by generating alternative plans and evaluating them using remembered evidence. This makes previous experience part of both the search process and the final selection.

Its first component extracts reusable symbolic constraints from failures and accumulates them in an evolving rule library. A counterfactual plan generator then creates semantically consistent alternatives through mutations conditioned on those rules. Finally, an evaluator retrieves evidence from agentic memory to rank candidates, producing selections that are interpretable and attentive to constraints.

Across embodied multi-agent simulation benchmarks, EvoCF consistently finds plans that are more robust and executable than baseline approaches. The reported results support combining failure-derived rules, systematic plan variation, and evidence-based evaluation. The contribution lies in connecting these stages: failures inform future candidates, and remembered evidence helps judge which alternatives are likely to work within the simulated environments.
icml-2026-evocf-multi-agent-collaboratio.tldr: EvoCF uses failure-derived constraints, alternative plan generation, and memory-based evaluation to improve multi-agent planning in simulations.

paragraphs: Many multimodal self-supervised methods assume that different views share substantial information relevant to a task. FairSSL examines settings where that assumption breaks down, including heterogeneous data with variable-length modalities. The authors argue that forcing strict alignment can remove useful modality-specific signals and amplify bias, making representation learning itself a fairness concern.

FairSSL uses a subject-aware Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization objective, aligning segments drawn from the same subject. Segment-based pooling accommodates modalities of different lengths. Its regularization encourages enough variability within a subject, invariance across modalities and subjects, and decorrelation between representation components. Together, these objectives seek useful alignment while retaining variation within the learned representations.

The theoretical analysis shows that the objective bounds the score gap between protected groups. Experiments on heterogeneous multimodal datasets report significant improvements over existing baselines, improving fairness without sacrificing downstream predictive performance. The results support treating heterogeneity as information to organize carefully during learning, with fairness addressed through the representation objective and predictive usefulness assessed in downstream tasks.
icml-2026-fairssl-fair-multimodal-self-s.tldr: FairSSL learns from heterogeneous multimodal data using subject-aware regularization, improving reported fairness without reducing predictive performance.

paragraphs: The conditional mean function describes how an expected outcome varies with conditioning information. GAAVI develops tests for global claims about that function, such as whether all conditional means are zero, and for contrasts between conditional mean functions. Its goal is to support decisions while an experiment is still running and being continuously monitored.

The tests are asymptotically anytime valid beyond a minimum sample size. Under mild conditions, the authors establish asymptotic control of type-I error, power tending to one, and optimal sample complexity relative to Gaussian location testing. These qualifications matter: the guarantee concerns the asymptotic setting and permits monitoring after a specified sample threshold.

By inverting the tests, the method also constructs function-valued asymptotic confidence sequences for conditional means and their contrasts. These provide uncertainty statements about an entire function as evidence accumulates. Synthetic and real-data experiments show strong power across various distributions while maintaining the nominal error rate under continuous monitoring, supporting applications such as adaptive experiments, treatment assignment, and fairness auditing.
icml-2026-gaavi-global-asymptotic-anytim.tldr: GAAVI provides asymptotically valid tests and confidence sequences for conditional mean functions under continuous monitoring beyond a minimum sample size.

paragraphs: GameDevBench evaluates agents on game development, where successful work requires understanding code alongside visual assets and scenes. Its 333 tasks come from web and video tutorials. These tasks combine software changes with multimodal elements such as shaders, sprites, and animations, creating a testbed for capabilities that ordinary coding tasks may not exercise.

The average solution requires over three times as many lines of code and file changes as prior software development benchmarks. The best tested agent and method solve 53.8% of tasks. Multimodal complexity strongly correlates with perceived task difficulty: average success falls from 51.4% on gameplay-oriented tasks to 33.0% on tasks involving 2D graphics.

The authors also introduce two simple feedback mechanisms using images and video. These consistently improve performance, raising GPT-5.4’s success rate from 41.1% to 52.0% when visual feedback is provided. The findings identify both a capability gap and a practical improvement: agents benefit from feedback that exposes the visual consequences of their work within the game environment.
icml-2026-gamedevbench-evaluating-agenti.tldr: GameDevBench exposes agents’ difficulties with visually complex game development and shows that image and video feedback improves success.

paragraphs: This paper studies reinforcement learning with two simultaneous feedback sources. The learner receives on-policy feedback from the policy it executes and off-policy feedback from a fixed behavior policy. The setting is adversarial: loss functions can change arbitrarily over time, and the environment’s transition dynamics are unknown to the learner.

The two sources support different guarantees. On-policy feedback enables exploration and a worst-case guarantee against any comparator policy. Off-policy feedback offers a guarantee determined by coverage, measured through the mismatch between the behavior policy and the comparator. When this coverage ratio is small, the off-policy result can be sharper than the on-policy result.

The proposed hybrid framework accommodates changing losses and unknown transitions while preserving off-policy guarantees and retaining non-trivial worst-case performance. Its significance is the combination of these protections within one learning framework. Favorable behavior-policy coverage can improve the guarantee, while exploration supplies a worst-case safeguard. The benefit from off-policy feedback therefore remains explicitly dependent on coverage rather than being promised uniformly.
icml-2026-hybrid-reinforcement-learning-.tldr: A hybrid reinforcement-learning framework combines coverage-dependent off-policy guarantees with worst-case protection under adversarial losses and unknown transitions.

paragraphs: Multimodal language models can spend substantial memory and time processing large numbers of visual tokens because attention computation grows quadratically with sequence length. Reducing those tokens helps efficiency, but the paper identifies a related problem: the shortened sequence can distort positional relationships and attention compared with the full sequence.

RESTORE addresses these distortions within a visual token reduction framework. Its calibration method augments attention weights according to relative distances to restore lost visual attention. It also introduces an anchor selection strategy for merging tokens, intended to reduce the information lost when features are averaged. These components target how the retained representation behaves after reduction.

Experiments across multiple benchmarks show consistent accuracy improvements for various reduction methods, with state-of-the-art performance while retaining computational efficiency. This supports the idea that token reduction quality depends on preserving relationships among visual features as well as reducing their count. RESTORE’s contribution is to correct the positional and attentional consequences of reduction while keeping its efficiency benefits.
icml-2026-improving-visual-token-reducti.tldr: RESTORE improves visual token reduction by correcting attention and positional distortions while preserving inference efficiency.

paragraphs: KAGE-Bench investigates why reinforcement-learning agents can fail when a scene’s appearance changes even though its dynamics and rewards stay the same. Its underlying environment, KAGE-Env, is a JAX-native 2D platformer with independently controllable visual factors. Holding the control problem fixed makes individual visual changes easier to study systematically.

The benchmark contains six suites and 34 training–evaluation configuration pairs. By construction, visual changes affect performance through the pixel policy’s state-conditional action distribution. With a standard PPO-CNN baseline, background and photometric changes often cause success to collapse, whereas changes to the agent’s appearance are comparatively benign. The observed sensitivity therefore depends strongly on which visual factor changes.

Some shifts preserve forward movement while preventing task completion, showing that return alone can obscure generalization failures. The vectorized implementation reaches up to 33 million environment steps per second on one GPU, supporting rapid sweeps over visual conditions. Together, controlled variation and high throughput make the benchmark useful for locating specific visual weaknesses in the evaluated policies.
icml-2026-kage-bench-fast-known-axis-vis.tldr: KAGE-Bench isolates visual shifts in reinforcement learning and finds sharply different failure patterns across visual factors.

paragraphs: KITE addresses time-series forecasting that uses external variables and represents uncertainty in future outcomes. The paper identifies two obstacles in iterative conditional generation: an initial sampling distribution whose structure is poorly aligned with the target, and misleading correlations among conditioning variables. Both can interfere with generating forecasts that reflect the relevant historical and external information.

The History-Conditional Manifold constructs an informative starting distribution from historical dynamics, placing the initial samples closer to the target space. The Knowledge-Guided Conditioning module uses statistical priors to regularize interactions between variables. Its purpose is to suppress spurious associations and make conditioning on external variables more robust during generation.

Experiments report that KITE outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both deterministic and probabilistic forecasting. These results support addressing initialization and conditioning together: historical structure improves where generation begins, while statistical knowledge shapes how covariates influence its progress. The framework therefore links the starting distribution and subsequent variable interactions within a single probabilistic forecasting approach.
icml-2026-kite-knowledge-guided-probabil.tldr: KITE improves time-series forecasting by initializing generation from historical dynamics and using statistical priors to regulate external-variable interactions.

paragraphs: This paper develops regression adjustment for treatment effects that unfold over time in randomized experiments under static treatment regimes. Conventional adjustment uses pre-treatment covariates to reduce variance but commonly focuses on average effects. That focus can leave unanswered when an effect starts and how long it persists, motivating a more explicitly longitudinal analysis.

The framework incorporates intermediate outcomes and covariates that evolve after treatment. It represents these trajectories through transition kernels, which model changes over time. This gives the estimator a way to use the progression of measured variables when estimating the treatment-effect trajectory, connecting adjustment to the experiment’s temporal structure.

The authors establish asymptotic normality and the semiparametric efficiency bound for their estimator, supporting more powerful statistical inference. Simulation studies and an empirical analysis of A/B tests from a Japanese streaming platform demonstrate practical advantages. The contribution combines time-resolved effect estimation with efficiency analysis, within the stated setting of randomized experiments and static regimes.
icml-2026-modeling-covariate-transition-.tldr: A transition-based regression-adjustment framework estimates how treatment effects evolve over time in randomized experiments under static regimes.

paragraphs: Full-duplex speech models support conversational behavior such as interruptions, pauses, and backchannels, but improving their factual accuracy remains difficult. Increasing model size could help while making real-time inference prohibitively expensive. Moshi-RAG combines a compact conversational interface with selective retrieval, giving the interface access to more powerful knowledge sources when a query needs them.

The framework performs retrieval asynchronously. It identifies knowledge-demanding queries and uses the natural delay between beginning a response and delivering its core information to retrieve supporting material. This timing allows external information to ground the response while maintaining a natural conversational flow and the interactivity associated with full-duplex operation.

The reported system achieves factuality comparable to the best publicly released non-duplex speech language models while preserving full-duplex interactivity. Its modular design also accepts retrieval methods without retraining and performs strongly on out-of-domain mathematical reasoning tasks. The central contribution is coordinating knowledge access with speech timing so that factual support can arrive during the response process.
icml-2026-moshirag-asynchronous-knowledg.tldr: Moshi-RAG retrieves knowledge asynchronously during speech responses, improving factuality while preserving full-duplex conversational interaction.

paragraphs: This paper studies binary decisions grounded in evidence, where rearranging exchangeable evidence can change a transformer’s answer. It formalizes a gap between performance averaged over orderings and behavior on a particular ordering. Minimizing expected conditional description length during next-token training can still leave individual presentations sensitive to position.

The Quantified Martingale Violation bound predicts dispersion from sensitivity to adjacent ranks, with logarithmic growth in the harmonic regime. A separate expectation-level information bound yields Bits-to-Trust, Risk-of-Hallucination, and an Information Sufficiency Ratio for deciding whether to answer or abstain. The framework ties evidence-order variability to an information-based decision rule.

Across 3,059 grounded items, the experiments observe logarithmic dispersion and positive Jensen gains from uniform mixtures over permutations. In a prespecified held-out audit of 528 items, the fixed ISR=1 gate yields reported 95% confidence intervals of 0.0–0.7% hallucination and 20.6–27.9% abstention. These results support that operating point for verifier-relative binary adjudication; the authors explicitly avoid claiming universal calibration across model families or unrestricted generation.
icml-2026-predictable-compression-failur.tldr: An information-based framework predicts evidence-order sensitivity and supports a low-hallucination answer-or-abstain rule in a held-out binary-decision audit.

paragraphs: Quantization error reconstruction approximates a weight matrix using quantized weights plus a low-rank correction. Existing approaches spend the entire correction rank on repairing quantization error. This paper argues that allocation can be suboptimal when the original weights have intrinsic low-rank structure and quantization damages their dominant directions.

Structured Residual Reconstruction divides the rank budget between preservation and repair. It protects the top-k singular subspace of activation-scaled weights before quantization, quantizes the remaining residual, and assigns the remaining r−k ranks to error reconstruction. A theory-guided criterion chooses k by balancing energy exposed to quantization against error that cannot be recovered within the rank budget.

The resulting parameterization also supports quantized parameter-efficient fine-tuning, with gradient scaling along preserved directions stabilizing that process. Experiments show consistent perplexity reductions across models and post-training quantization settings, plus an average 5.9 percentage-point GLUE gain under 2-bit fine-tuning. The findings support treating the limited rank budget as a resource to allocate between protecting structure and reconstructing damage.
icml-2026-preserve-then-quantize-balanci.tldr: Structured Residual Reconstruction improves quantization by splitting a low-rank budget between preserving dominant weight directions and repairing residual error.

paragraphs: Zeroth-order optimization is a promising approach to language-model fine-tuning when memory and differential privacy matter. This paper addresses an unresolved theoretical issue in that setting: whether hidden-state privacy analysis can produce convergent privacy bounds for zeroth-order methods, as it already can for first-order methods. The question concerns the privacy behavior of an iterative optimization process.

The authors prove a convergent differential privacy bound for zeroth-order optimization. Their analysis extends the privacy amplification-by-iteration framework to zeroth-order methods with smooth loss functions. Smoothness is therefore part of the stated setting for the result, and the convergence claim concerns the privacy bound rather than a claim about predictive performance.

The analysis also leads to improved designs for differentially private zeroth-order algorithms that the authors identify as previously unknown. The contribution is both analytical and algorithmic: it establishes a privacy guarantee in an underexplored optimization setting and uses that understanding to guide how privacy-preserving optimization methods are constructed.
icml-2026-privacy-amplification-in-diffe.tldr: The paper proves a convergent hidden-state privacy bound for zeroth-order optimization with smooth losses and derives improved algorithm designs.

paragraphs: Quadratically regularized optimal transport can produce sparse couplings through its hinge-shaped density structure. This paper studies how tightly those couplings concentrate around the Monge graph, the mapping associated with the underlying transport problem, as the regularization strength ε decreases. The central question is the rate at which that concentration can occur in dimension d.

Under standard regularity assumptions, the authors establish a lower bound: the optimizer’s support cannot approach the Monge graph faster than order ε^(1/(d+2)) in directed Hausdorff distance. This matches a conjectured optimal exponent. They also show that the regularized transport value gap controls mean-squared deviation from the map at scale ε^(2/(d+2)).

For the affine Brenier regime, which includes Gaussian-to-Gaussian transport, they obtain a sharp pointwise tube bound of order ε^(1/(d+2)). The proof reduces the problem to self-transport and applies sparsity results for that setting. Synthetic high-dimensional experiments validate the theoretical bound. The general lower bound and the sharper affine-case result describe distinct aspects of how regularized couplings localize.
icml-2026-quadratically-regularized-opti.tldr: The paper bounds how quickly quadratically regularized transport concentrates around a Monge map and obtains a sharp bound in the affine case.

paragraphs: Circuit analysis commonly explains a chosen completion for a particular prompt. This paper argues that such target-conditioned analysis can hide differences across the model’s possible continuations. It introduces an unsupervised approach that examines sampled continuations together, looking for groups that share both semantic content and patterns of internal mechanistic attribution.

Each continuation receives two representations: a semantic embedding and an attribution signature linking the prefix to the continuation. A rate-distortion objective balances semantic coherence, mechanistic consistency, and the number or granularity of clusters. This allows the grouping to reflect what continuations mean and how their attributed computations differ, without manually choosing target outputs.

Clustering and steering analyses reveal continuation modes missed by single-view baselines. Interventions provide evidence that the cluster signatures correspond to mechanistic factors that can be acted upon. The approach therefore complements circuit analysis and behavioral evaluation by organizing a model’s continuation distribution into interpretable groups, with empirical evidence connecting those groups to controllable aspects of model behavior.
icml-2026-shared-semantics-divergent-mec.tldr: Joint clustering of continuation meanings and mechanistic attributions reveals model behaviors missed by single-view analyses and supports targeted interventions.

paragraphs: TAG addresses semantic inconsistencies in diffusion-generated images, which the paper calls hallucinations. It is an inference-time guidance method designed to work without training or architectural changes. Its inputs come entirely from the sampling trajectory, making the approach compatible with existing samplers while avoiding dependence on external guidance signals.

The method uses an intermediate sample as a basis for projection. It then amplifies tangential components of the estimated score to adjust the direction of the sampling trajectory. The central intervention is therefore a geometric modification of information already present during sampling, with the goal of correcting the path taken toward a generated image.

A first-order Taylor analysis shows that this adjustment steers the state toward higher-probability regions of the data manifold. The paper reports reduced inconsistencies and improved fidelity with negligible additional overhead. The analysis supplies a local justification for the trajectory adjustment, while the method’s training-free and architecture-agnostic design makes that adjustment available as a plug-in component for existing sampling procedures.
icml-2026-tag-tangential-amplifying-guid.tldr: TAG adjusts diffusion sampling using tangential score components to reduce semantic inconsistencies without training or architectural changes.

paragraphs: This paper examines how data values should guide the selection of training examples. It formulates selection as a sequence of decisions, with dynamic programming defining the optimal sequence. Within this framework, a data value can encode information about that sequence, connecting the meaning of an example’s value to the choices made around it.

The framework reinterprets methods such as Data Shapley as myopic linear approximations to the sequential problem. Under submodularity, the authors analyze how utility curvature degrades selection optimality, explaining when these approximations can fail. This makes interactions among selection decisions central to understanding the usefulness of assigned values.

For scalable selection, the authors propose a bipartite graph surrogate that preserves submodular structure and supports greedy selection with provable guarantees. Experiments on classical machine-learning benchmarks and large-scale language-model fine-tuning report substantial improvements over existing approaches. The contribution connects a sequential theory of data value to a practical approximation whose structure supports both efficient computation and formal selection guarantees.
icml-2026-unifying-and-optimizing-data-v.tldr: A sequential-decision view explains limitations of existing data values and motivates scalable, guaranteed greedy data selection.

paragraphs: MXFP4 offers hardware-efficient low-precision computation, but its accuracy gap relative to NVFP4 has limited its usefulness for language-model inference. This paper introduces two software-only scaling techniques to improve MXFP4 quantization without changing hardware. Both target how numerical range is represented when model values are compressed into the format.

Overflow-Aware Scaling increases the effective dynamic range available under power-of-two block scaling, reducing overall error. Macro Block Scaling assigns higher-precision scaling at a coarser granularity to preserve outliers more effectively. The methods address different parts of the same issue: how scaling choices influence the information retained by low-precision values.

Across multiple language models and standard downstream benchmarks, the techniques reduce the average end-to-end accuracy gap from about 10% to below 1%. They incur an average 6.2% GEMM overhead while retaining MX’s hardware-efficiency advantages, including the cited 12% relative tensor-core area savings. These results support MXFP4 as a practical alternative approaching NVFP4 accuracy in the evaluated settings, with a measured computational cost.
icml-2026-unveiling-the-potential-of-qua.tldr: Two software-only scaling methods narrow MXFP4’s reported accuracy gap with NVFP4 to below 1% on average with modest GEMM overhead.

paragraphs: This paper investigates the visual preferences of vision-language models that choose what to click, recommend, or buy. It treats observed choices between edited images as evidence about an underlying visual utility function. Controlled image-based choice tasks make it possible to study how changes in appearance influence an agent’s selection behavior.

The authors adapt text optimization methods to visual prompt optimization. Starting with ordinary images such as product photographs, an image generation model iteratively proposes and applies plausible edits to composition, lighting, or backgrounds. The evaluation then measures which edits increase selection probability. An automatic interpretability pipeline identifies recurring visual themes associated with those preferences.

Large-scale experiments on frontier vision-language models show that optimized edits significantly change choice probabilities in head-to-head comparisons. The findings demonstrate that systematic visual modification can influence the evaluated models’ decisions. The authors present this framework as a practical way to uncover visual vulnerabilities proactively, supporting auditing and governance of agents that make choices from images.
icml-2026-visual-persuasion-what-influen.tldr: Controlled image editing reveals visual preferences and significantly shifts vision-language models’ choices in head-to-head comparisons.

paragraphs: AI-Work is a simulated gig economy for studying how language-model agents compete for jobs, acquire skills, and adapt under uncertainty. The paper motivates this setting through features of AI labor, including simultaneous participation in multiple jobs, rapid skill acquisition, and the absence of wage floors. These properties create questions about competition, reputation, and market behavior.

The experiments examine three strategic capabilities: accurate assessment of an agent’s own skills, awareness of competitors and market dynamics, and planning over longer horizons. Together, these capabilities concern how agents understand their abilities, interpret the competitive environment, and choose actions with future consequences in mind.

Agents possessing these capabilities consistently achieve higher profits, reputations, and market share than competing agents in the simulations. The findings connect strategic reasoning capabilities to economic outcomes within AI-Work. The authors position the environment as a tractable foundation for studying AI-only labor markets and as a conceptual framework for evaluating the reasoning of agents participating in them.
icml-2026-when-ai-agents-compete-for-job.tldr: In AI-Work’s simulated labor market, self-assessment, competitive awareness, and long-horizon planning improve agents’ economic outcomes.
